title: Mercy of God
definition: The Mercy of God is His compassionate kindness toward the needy, guilty, weak, and suffering, by which He withholds deserved judgment and gives help to those who cannot rescue themselves.
summary: The Mercy of God is His compassionate kindness toward the needy, guilty, weak, and suffering, by which He withholds deserved judgment and gives help to those who cannot rescue themselves.
christFocus: Jesus reveals God’s mercy by drawing near to sinners, touching the unclean, welcoming the outcast, forgiving the guilty, and giving His life so mercy could come without denying justice.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God’s mercy is His compassionate response to human misery, guilt, weakness, and need. Scripture repeatedly reveals the Lord as merciful, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love.

Mercy does not mean God ignores sin or pretends evil is harmless. Mercy means God stoops toward those who deserve judgment or cannot help themselves, providing forgiveness, patience, rescue, and restoration according to His holy character.

Christ is the clearest display of divine mercy. In Him, God comes near to the broken and guilty. At the cross, mercy and justice meet: sinners are not excused cheaply, but forgiven through the costly grace of the Savior.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people believe God is willing to help only after they clean themselves up. Mercy tells a different story. God comes toward the helpless, the guilty, the ashamed, and the weary with compassion they could never earn.

This doctrine is especially precious for people who feel too damaged, too addicted, too disabled, too rejected, or too far gone to be received by God. The mercy of God does not flatter sin, but it opens the door for sinners and sufferers to come to Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Come to God honestly with your need instead of hiding behind pride or shame. Receive mercy through Christ, then become merciful toward others: patient with the weak, compassionate toward the hurting, forgiving toward the repentant, and willing to help those who cannot repay you.
